newsitem.title: GERMANY: MCC denies new "Smart" car prototype unstable.
newsitem.headline: MCC denies new "Smart" car prototype unstable.

text.p: Micro Compact Car AG (MCC), a joint venture including Mercedes-Benz AG to produce the new "Smart" model car, denied on Wednesday press reports that the new vehicle was unstable and dangerous.
The German magazine "Auto Motor und Sport" reported in its latest editions that the "Smart" had tipped over in tests and quoted parts suppliers as saying the car had flipped more than once.
The Smart is a small new city car being developed by Daimler-Benz and Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horologerie (SMH) and is due to go on sale in 1998.
An MCC spokeswoman said the company had intentially tipped the car over as part of its routine test track studies and that it did not suffer any stability problems.
"We tried to see where the car would tip," she said. "There is no question of safety."
Auto Motor und Sport said the Smart had tipped because it has a high center of gravity for a vehicle with small tyres.
